notes.title: Well toot my lizards, Void Bastards is rustling up a space-western sequel
notes.content:
'The Wild Bastards' is about the best name I've heard for a gang of alien outlaws in a space-western, good enough that let's skip past the fact that the game was announced last year and we've only just noticed. Wild Bastards is the follow-up to Void Bastards, 2019's roguelikelike first-person shooter about a prisoner in a corporate nightmare forced to raid derelict spaceships on a wild goose chase. This time, it's leaning into crime, jaunting across the galaxy to resurrect a game of legendary outlaws, the Wild Bastards. Allow me to repeat that name: the Wild Bastards. Alright, now come watch the gameplay trailer.

notes.title: Humble drops its monthly bundle prices (yay), introduces its own PC launcher (boo)
notes.content:
Humble has been heavily experimenting with how to present its bundles since Humble Monthly was ended in favour of Humble Choice, and the response from long-time users of the store have been mixed. Now prices are dropping for that bundle starting in February, and as part of the revamp, Humble is trying to add yet another app to your ever-growing collection of PC game launchers.

Starting with the February bundle, the Humble Choice price is dropping to $11.99 USD, and that single price will get you access to every game in the collection. "The exact number of games might vary each month", but you will keep permanent access to any games you've picked up through the bundle. Keys for these games will continue to be provided through keys for platforms like Steam, Origin, Epic, and GOG.

Then there's the Humble app. Through this app, Humble will provide access to a Game Pass-style selection of games for the duration of your subscription, starting with Forager, Wizard of Legend, Dodgeball Academia, Unsighted, and Void Bastards. The old Humble Trove is becoming the Vault, which will continue to offer a selection of DRM-free bonus indie games, as always.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Yooka-Laylee and Void Bastards are currently free on the Epic Games Store
notes.content:
If you're looking for a couple more video game freebies to shove unceremoniously into your almost certainly already overstuffed 'to do' pile, Epic has you covered, with Yooka-Laylee and Void Bastards currently free on its PC store.

Yooka-Laylee, if you're unfamiliar, is a spiritual successor to Rare's beloved platformer Banjo-Kazooie - and was developed by Playtonic, a studio founded by a number of ex-Rare veterans. Lizard and bat replace bear and bird in Yooka-Laylee, but the formula will be immediately familiar to Banjo-Kazooie fans, setting players loose across a number of sprawling, predominantly platforming-focussed worlds as they embark on an perky, old-school collectathon in search of missing Quills.

All in all, it's a decently entertaining adventure (although its superb side-scrolling sequel, Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair, is far superior), and one that Eurogamer contributor Edwin Evans-Thirlwell called a "sumptuous, diverting homage to a bygone era in game design that should keep fans of the old school hooked, even if it doesn't set the world on fire."

Read more

notes.title: Prime Gaming's free games haul for January includes Void Bastards
notes.content:
If you're an Amazon Prime subscriber, you just got some new free PC games. January's selection of free games is now available, and this first batch of 2021 includes the graphic novel-inspired FPS game Void Bastards.

In Void Bastards, you lead a team of misfits out of the Sargasso Nebula, creeping through derelict space frigates, using a blend of tactical decisions and sharpshooting to fend off the many dangers you'll discover within. There's a rewarding strategy layer to the action, as you'll be plotting your course through the nebula, picking your team's next location as well as your squad and loadout.

This month's bundle also includes engineering-based physical comedy games Bridge Constructor Playground and When Ski Lifts Go Wrong, both of which involve piecing together nominally safe spans for vehicles and skiers to cross. Of course, half the fun is watching what happens when structures fail, so prepare to enjoy many scenes of trucks plummeting into rivers and snowmobilers pancaking against cliff faces when your plans don't quite work out.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Game devs and players continue banding together to help the Australian bushfire crisis
notes.content:
Australia is still burning, but over the last couple of days they’ve actually had some rain! While this is a big help to certain areas, there are still 83 fires blazing around the country, and there’s a lot of people and wildlife still in trouble. It’s good job then that there are even more game devs, companies, and communities banding together to help out our friends down under.

A new Humble Bundle, a donation from the makers of Warframe, and a charity initiative run by Eve Online players are just three more ways the games industry is raising money, and you can get involved to show your support too.

notes.title: Void Bastards cleans up with Bang Tydy DLC and free workplace challenges
notes.content:
Void Bastards was a right laugh, yeah? I had a proper good time blasting my way around the daftest comic 2000AD never made earlier this year, but it did get a little stale after a bit. There’s only so many times a chavvy wee sod can tell you to shove a blaster up your arse before it starts to grate, y’know. Even if it’s a lark for a few evenings, Graham felt it needed a bit more direction in his review. Today’s Bang Tidy update might not reinvent that wheel, but it does shove a few more cats into the mix to keep things interesting.

[i]Product recall notice: Tydybot and Tydierbot. Attention consumers, Tydy has issued a product recall notice for our popular cleaning robots. There is no need to be alarmed, however, consumers should avoid wearing orange clothing in the vicinity of a Tydybot that has not yet been recalled for reprogramming. Tydy’s sophisticated cleaning AI has been found to identify orange clothing as dirty, dirty mess that must be vacuumed away. Tydy cannot be held responsible for asphyxiation, detached eyeballs or damaged clothing that results from ignoring this safety warning![/i]

On [b]Tydy[/b] ships, you’ll find [b]Tydybots[/b]. notes.title: Podcast: The best game cities, from Dunwall to Kamurocho
notes.content:
Rural life is disgusting. All those shrubs and trees, how awful. You should pack your checkered pouch and head into the big smoke. The shining cities of videogameland are calling to you, and the team of the RPS podcast, the Electronic Wireless Show, will be there to help you get settled in to your disgusting, overpriced flat no matter which giant urban maze you choose. Trust us, life is so much better in the city.

Ignore the rats. You’ll get used to them.

notes.title: NEW TYDY SHIP MODULE - WELCOME TO THE COMBUSTION CHAMBER

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33915034/83e80279cd55af7dbe7cd8f4c881fc7462ea9d3a.gif[/img]

[i]Attention spacefarers! Everyone knows that nebula radiation really dries out your skin, but did you also know that’s it is highly mutagenic? Even worse, if your spacecraft is full of mutants, it’s likely also full of dirty, messy junk! 

Why not let Tydy clean your vessel? Our bots collect junk and then transport it in our custom Tydy vans to a Tydy Furnace ship where it is incinerated in our safe and environmentally sensitive combustion chambers![/i]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33915034/de32f9363f034cc3074f808e71d213533b2de2af.gif[/img]

Are you almost dead? Life support system critical? Don’t have the necessary parts to build a [b]Heart Starter[/b] and revive yourself? The all new [b]Combustion Chamber[/b] has you covered.

Ships equipped with a [b]Combustion Chamber[/b] have a [b]furnace passcard [/b]stashed somewhere on the ship. Find it, and it’ll give you access to the [b]furnace[/b]. Inside is a glorious [b]Heart Starter[/b]! Unfortunately for you, looks like someone left the furnace on, so hopefully you’ll have enough health left to wade through a bit of fire first.

notes.title: Addendum: New content for Void Bastards
notes.content:
[i]Dear client, we have recently received a number of submissions of Form 93-Q: request for additional information pursuant to upcoming software updates. Although “additional information” can be dangerous for most clients, our busy scribes have a response which you may read below. Be aware that Form 93-Q has now been discontinued and is replaced by Form 93-R*.  [/i]

Some of you have been asking what exactly is going to be in our first big content update, what exactly is it called and when it’s going to be released.

The update is [i]Workplace Challenges[/i], not [i]Nemesis[/i], as you may have read in some places. It includes the following content which we’ll be detailing over the coming few weeks:

[list]
[*] The workplace challenges themselves, which challenge you to complete the game under new rules that will force you to play differently (and smarter). These challenges will be free for all players.
[/list]
[list]
[*] The Tydy DLC which includes an entirely new organisation with its own ships, a new opponent and a new weapon. This DLC will be paid for (price still TBD). Don’t worry, it won’t be very much.
[/list]
[list]
[*] Extra content for the main game including a new opponent, many new ship types and more. This content will also be free!
[/list]

That just leaves the question of release date, to which the answer is: soon but we don’t know exactly when yet as we haven’t finished making all of the above (also we’re trying to get some sleep after shipping the game last month).

[i]* Form 93-R not yet available due to paper shortages. [/i]

notes.title: VOID BASTARDS - CHALLENGE MODES + DLC?! HELL YES.
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33915034/9906d1196616c5a548f2f8b0e381b98ce32bf391.gif[/img]

[i]Dear Client,

Thank you for cooperating with WCG administrative procedures to facilitate the return of the Void Ark. Your performance has been noted and we are pleased to inform you that additional workplace challenges are now being prepared. These challenges will test your occupational competencies as never before! Can you lift your KPIs and push your personal performance envelope to the limit?[/i]

Hey everyone! We know you’ve been hankering for some new content for Void Bastards. We heard you, and we’ll be rolling out some [b]FREE[/b] challenge modes to completely change the way you navigate through the Sargasso Nebula. We're still ironing out the details but expect challenges like: stealthing your way past super tough enemies, being forced to rely on amped up authorisation skills to take over ship systems and managing a super fast but hard to control client. Did we mention this will all be [b]FREE[/b]?

Warning: don’t stand too near a Tydy Bot as their dirt recognition units have been known to malfunction when exposed to nebula radiation.[/i]

Welcome to the first patch for Void Bastards, released today June 6! We've been listening to feedback and problems and attempting to address the most urgent issues and we'll be continuing to support the game from here on out.

[b]New Features[/b]
[list]
[*] Added option to change border colour to black or grey instead of white.
[*] Added option to adjust gamma.
[*] Quitting the game while on board a ship no longer kills your character. If you exit the game, return to the main menu or the game crashes while on board a ship you will be able to resume from just prior to boarding that ship.
[/list]

[list]
[*] Various attempted fixes to issue where weapon sprites become giant and camera gets locked in place.
[*] Fixed amounts in the various health upgrade descriptions.
[*] Fixed wording in health upgrade description (Russian).
[*] Fixed a portrait that had two sets of hair.
[*] Moved turret projectile spawn so that it is no longer possible to stand right next to a turret and be safe.
[*] Fixed oxygen terminal giving too much oxygen.
[*] Vsync default setting is applied correctly (before vsync is changed in options).
[*] Fixed progress part location arrow disappearing when a target ship is in the exact center of the nebula map.
[*] Fixed occasional issue where progress and locater arrows point to the same ship but one moves to another location when you arrive at that ship.
[*] Fixed ammo count overflowing when you have four digits worth of ammo.
[*] Adjusted collision mesh on round table to help player getting stuck on it.
[*] Removed “good source of staples” from the description for the CNT Tax Boat.

[*] Don’t show the BACS prompt to build a glow bulb if you have already built the part locater.
[*] Don’t allow bringing up the full screen map over the introductory screen at the start of the tutorial.
[*] Removed some couches that created a small gap that the player could get stuck in in the spin and win module.
[*] Stop radiation audio feedback when you are incurring radiation from an irradiated enemy and that enemy dies.

[/list]

notes.title: Void Bastards challenges loons to conquer space with a foon
notes.content:
According to some, who shall go unnamed, rogue-y FPS Void Bastards is too easy a game even if you crank its difficulty slider all the way up to the amusingly named ‘Hard Bastard’ mode. Developers Blue Manchu are obviously listening to them, because they’ve just added a new super-high-end challenge mode to the game. Unlocked by completing the game on Hard Bastard mode with the Ironman modifier, Foon mode asks you to do it all again, this time armed with nothing but a piece of cheap plastic space-cutlery. See how it works in a cheeky trailer below.

notes.title: VOID BASTARDS EXTRA MODE - FOON UNLOCKED!
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33915034/d4b51e03cebc3ce45709e580792d3dd29bf6fc44.png[/img]

Looking for an extra challenge? We’ve got you covered.

If you thought Ironman difficulty was tough, wait until you unlock the Foon. Here’s how you do it:

1. Finish Void Bastards on any difficulty to unlock Ironman difficulty
2. Finish Void Bastards on Hard Bastard + Ironman 
3. You’ve unlocked the Foon game modifier
4. Start a new game
5. Enjoy your newfound cutlery

Foon mode allows you to ONLY use the Foon. No other weapons or devices can be used.

The upside is that the Foon allows you to backstab for one hit kills! Otherwise, it just does 10 damage. You might have a hard time with Secbots and Peepers.

Good luck, client.

notes.title: Wot I Think: Void Bastards
notes.content:
Developer: Blue Manchu
Publisher: Humble

Release: Out now
On: Windows, MacOSX
From: Steam, Humble
For: 25/$30/ 30

If Gone Home is the answer to the question, “What if BioShock without guns?”, then Void Bastards is the answer to the question, “What if BioShock without story?” On a series of post-disaster spaceships, each rendered in a slick comic book style, you fight or avoid grumpy mutants, circumvent security systems, hack turrets, and rummage through bins like yer da after that time he accidentally threw away all his Euros on a Spanish holiday. Your motivating force on this hazardous journey isn’t to hear more dialogue from Andrew Ryan or SHODAN, but to serve systems borrowed from the likes of FTL, Rogue Legacy, and other modern roguelites. It works: I am motivated.

notes.title: Stylish shooter Void Bastards will splice BioShock gameplay and Borderlands art in May
notes.content:
Void Bastards looks like a mash-up of all the best things: it's got the cel-shaded, sci-fi art style of a Borderlands title, gameplay mechanics inspired by BioShock, and dark humour to make even GLaDOS blush. If all that sounds good to you, thankfully you won't have to wait much longer, as Void Bastards is releasing on PC and Xbox One at the end of the month. Mark 29th May on your calendars.

The game is the latest project by Blue Manchu, the studio led by the former design director for BioShock and System Shock 2, Jonathan Chey. Unsurprisingly, he cites both titles as inspiration for Void Bastards, explaining much of the game design choices stem from those titles.

"I love the deep simulational gameplay of BioShock and System Shock 2 - they aren't just run and gun shooters," Chey says in the press release. "I wanted to find a way to experience more of that gameplay without having to replay the same story over and over. Wrapping the shooter inside a strategy game turned out to be a great way to do that!"

Read more

notes.title: Void Bastards warps in on May 29th
notes.content:
Void Bastards, the strategic roguelike-ish shooter from Blue Manchu now has a release date, broadcast to us through the uncaring depths of the internet: May 29th. Inspired by System Shock 2 and Bioshock (and from the design director on both), it’s a darkly humoured stealthy FPS designed to force hard strategic decisions as you make your way across an FTL-esque star-map full of hazards. Resources of all kinds are limited, and every shot fired on a mission is one that you might need later. All of this wrapped up in a nifty comic-book aesthetic. See the announcement trailer below.
